ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, it is known that line AD $\parallel$ BC, and BE bisects $\angle ABC$ and intersects line DA at point E. If $\angle DAB=54^\circ$, what is the value of $\angle E$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution}: Since AD$\parallel$BC,\\
it follows that $\angle$ABC=$\angle$DAB=54$^\circ$, $\angle$EBC=$\angle$E,\\
since BE bisects $\angle$ABC,\\
it follows that $\angle$EBC= $\frac{1}{2}$ $\angle$ABC=27$^\circ$,\\
hence, $\angle$E=\boxed{27^\circ}.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the upper part of the figure there is a straight line, and points D, A, E are on the same straight line; below there are points B, C, and BC is a horizontal line. Line segment AB goes obliquely upward from B to A, line segment BE goes obliquely upward from B to E, and the required angle E is the angle at point E formed by EA and EB, namely ∠AEB. Reasoning: It is known that AD ∥ BC, and AB is a transversal, so ∠DAB and ∠ABC are equal angles in a corresponding/alternate interior relationship. Therefore ∠ABC = 54°. Also because BE bisects ∠ABC, ∠EBC = 54° ÷ 2 = 27°. Since AE and AD are on the same straight line, and AD ∥ BC, AE ∥ BC. Taking BE as the transversal, ∠AEB is equal to ∠EBC, therefore ∠E = 27°.

raw_record.question_text: As shown in the diagram, line AD is parallel to BC, and BE bisects \(\angle ABC\) and intersects line DA at point E. If \(\angle DAB = 54^\circ\), what is the value of \(\angle E\)?

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: D, A, and E lie on the same straight top line; B and C lie on the bottom line; AB and BE are slanted segments from B, and the requested angle E is the angle between EA and EB, i.e. ∠AEB. From the text, use AD ∥ BC, BE bisects ∠ABC, and ∠DAB = 54°. Because AD is parallel to BC and AB is a transversal, ∠DAB equals ∠ABC. Thus ∠ABC = 54°. Since BE bisects ∠ABC, ∠EBC = 27°. Finally, because AE lies on the same line as AD and AD ∥ BC, the angle between EB and EA equals the corresponding/alternate angle between EB and BC, so ∠AEB = ∠EBC = 27°.
